From 1953 until 2018, a budget commission drafted Fulton's budget.
Its members were the Board chairman, the county manager and the chief financial officer.
In 2018, the Board gave that job to the county manager alone.
Resolution 26-0460, adopted Aug 5, 2026, brought a commission back "in a modified form."
Commissioner Ellis and Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman sponsored it.
The new commission's members are the county manager, the chief financial officer, Commissioner Bob Ellis (north) and Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman (south).
The county manager and chief financial officer still prepare the budget documents and ask departments for their budget proposals.
The commission works by agreement; if it can't agree, the county manager decides how to present the draft.
The two commissioner members are chosen before each budget cycle at a publicly announced Board meeting.
One comes from districts 1 to 3, and one from districts 4 to 6.
To be eligible, a member must have served a year, and must not have a term ending in the year the budget is drafted.
The rules have a fallback if no one in a group is eligible.
An eligible vice chair serves automatically.
For the 2027 budget, Ellis was the only eligible member from districts 1 to 3.
The two commissioners must ask all commissioners for their budget priorities.
They take part in reviewing departments' requests, and they report to the full Board.

units.t: Section 2-261 of the county code says the proposal "shall include the budget requests of all of the county's departments, agencies, elected officials and authorities."

units.t: Commissioner Bob Ellis and Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman sponsored Resolution 26-0460.

P-001.text: A RESOLUTION BY THE FULTON COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS, TO RE- ESTABLISH A BUDGET COMMISSION TO ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE COUNTY'S ANNUAL BUDGET; TO PROVIDE FOR ITS PURPOSE, COMPOSITION, SELECTION, ELIGIBILITY, AND DUTIES; TO AMEND SECTION 2-261 OF THE FULTON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES; TO ADD SECTION 2-263 OF THE FULTON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES; TO REPEAL CONFLICTING RESOLUTIONS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.

P-002.text: WHEREAS, from 1953 until 2016, Fulton County’s budgeting process was prescribed by a 1953 local law applicable to densely populated counties and enacted by the Georgia General Assembly (1953 Ga. L. 2815), which entrusted the creation and proposal of the annual budgets to a county budget commission; and WHEREAS, the budget commission consisted of the individuals holding the county positions (as they are known currently) of the chairman of the board of commissioners, the county manager, and the chief financial officer; and WHEREAS, in 2016, the Georgia General Assembly repealed the 1953 local law, which had the effect of authorizing Fulton County to establish its own budget ordinance pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-81-3; and WHEREAS, on June 15, 2016, Fulton County enacted a budget ordinance at Fulton County Code (“FCC”) Sec. 2-261 and 2-262 through Resolution 16-0465, to establish a process for the proposal and adoption of the budget and to ensure expenditures are made in accordance with the budget; and WHEREAS, the 2016 budget ordinance maintained the use of a budget commission composed of the chairman of the board of commissioners, the county manager, and the chief financial officer; and

P-003.text: WHEREAS, on August 15, 2018, through Resolution 18-0577 (the “Prior Budget Resolution”), the Board of Commissioners (“BOC”) opted to replace the budget commission with a process, codified in FCC Section 2-261, where the county manager solely creates and submits the proposed budget but is directed to “include the budget requests of all of the county’s departments, agencies, elected officials, and authorities” along with the proposed budget; and

P-004.locator: p.2, lines 7-14 (stated purpose of the change)
P-004.text: WHEREAS, the Board determines that it is in the best interest of Fulton County to reconstitute a Budget Commission in a modified form that combines the administrative and financial expertise of the County Manager and Chief Financial Officer with earlier and ongoing input from members of the Board, structured to ensure balanced representation from both the northern and southern portions of Fulton County; and WHEREAS, the Board desires to establish clear procedures governing the composition, selection, eligibility, and duties of such Budget Commission, while preserving the full Board's exclusive authority to adopt the County's annual budget.

P-005.locator: pp.2-3, Sec. 2-261 as amended, first paragraph (as adopted: struck words dropped)
P-005.text: Sec. 2-261, - Proposal and adoption of the budget. The budget commission shall submit or cause to be submitted annually to the board of commissioners, by no later than November 15, a proposed budget governing expenditures of all county funds, including capital outlay and public works projects, for the following year. The budget commission’s submission of the proposed budget shall include the budget requests of all of the county's departments, agencies, elected officials and authorities who receive funding from the county through the budget process. This proposed budget will serve, as presented, as the operating budget until a final budget is adopted. The procedures for budget preparation, submission to the governing authority, review by the governing authority, public review, notice, and hearings shall be as provided for in Chapter 81 of Title 36 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36-81-1 et seq.]. The budget shall then be adopted by the board of commissioners by no later than the second regular meeting in January of the year to which it applies, which budget, when so adopted by the board of commissioners, shall constitute the board of commissioners' appropriation of all funds for such year.
P-005.note: Removed the page number '[2]' that falls inside the span at the page break. 'county manager' is struck through on lines 19 and 23 (checked visually on a rendered page image).

P-006.locator: p.3, lines 9-22, Sec. 2-261 as amended, second paragraph
P-006.text: The county manager is authorized to take all administrative steps necessary to implement the budget as approved. The budget so adopted may be revised during the year only by formal action of the board of commissioners in a regular meeting which has been advertised in accordance with subsection (e) of Code Section 36-81-5 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36-81-5] and no increase shall be made in such budget without provision also being made for financing such increase. The proposed budget submitted by the budget commission shall be accompanied by a report containing information and data required by subsection (b) of Code Section 36-81-5 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36-81- 5]. A copy of the proposed budget shall be transmitted to the county clerk of the commission of Fulton County on the date it is submitted to the board of commissioners. Upon adoption of the budget, a copy shall be transmitted to the county clerk of the commission of Fulton County.

P-007.text: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Fulton County Board of Commissioners hereby adopts a new section of the Fulton County Code, Section 2-263. – Budget commission., outlining the purpose, composition, selection, eligibility and duties of the budget commission, as follows: Section 2-263. – Budget commission. (a) Purpose. The purpose of the budget commission is to assist in the development of the county's proposed annual operating and capital budgets by combining the professional expertise of the county manager and chief financial officer with the policy priorities of the full board of commissioners, as represented by two commissioners selected in accordance with this code section.

P-008.text: (b) Composition. The budget commission shall be composed of four (4) members: (1) The county manager; (2) The chief financial officer; (3) One member of the board of commissioners representing commission district 1, 2, or 3 (the “Northern Representative”); and (4) One member of the board of commissioners representing commission district 4, 5, or 6 (the “Southern Representative”).
P-008.note: Removed the page number '[3]' at the page break.

P-009.text: (c) Selection of commissioner members. (1) Prior to the commencement of each annual budget development cycle, the commissioners representing Districts 1, 2, and 3 shall meet and, by majority vote of those three members, nominate and select one of their number to serve as the Northern Representative for that cycle. (2) Prior to the commencement of each annual budget development cycle, the commissioners representing Districts 4, 5, and 6 shall meet and, by majority vote of those three members, nominate and select one of their number to serve as the Southern Representative for that cycle. (3) Selection under this code section shall occur at a regularly scheduled and duly noticed board of commissioners meeting, and the result shall be entered into the official minutes of the board of commissioners. (4) Where application of the Eligibility code subsection (d) leaves only one eligible commissioner within a district grouping described in paragraph (1) or (2) of this subsection, that commissioner shall serve as the applicable Representative without the necessity of nomination or vote.

P-010.text: (d) Eligibility; election-year exclusion. (1) A commissioner shall have served on the board of commissioners for at least one (1) year to be eligible to serve on the budget commission. (2) A commissioner whose current term of office expires in the same calendar year in which the budget commission is developing the budget for the forthcoming fiscal year shall not be eligible to serve as the Northern Representative or Southern Representative for that budget cycle. i. By way of illustration, a commissioner whose term expires in 2026 shall not be eligible to serve on the budget commission convened to develop the Fiscal Year 2027 budget, notwithstanding that such development begins in 2026 and continues into 2027. (3) In the event that every commissioner within a district grouping described in paragraphs (c)(1) or (c)(2) is simultaneously ineligible under this section for a given budget cycle, the full board of commissioners shall, by majority vote, either (i) permit the immediately preceding Northern Representative or Southern Representative, as applicable, to continue to serve in a holdover capacity for that cycle, or (ii) select a Representative from among the sitting commissioners representing that district grouping, notwithstanding the exclusion in paragraph (2) of this subsection.

P-011.text: (e) Vice chair. (1) If the vice chair of the board of commissioners is not, in a given budget cycle, ineligible under subsection (d), the vice chair shall automatically serve as the Northern Representative or Southern Representative, as applicable based on the vice chair’s district, without the necessity of nomination or election under subsection (c). (2) If the vice chair is ineligible under subsection (d) for a given budget cycle, the vice chair shall be excluded from service on the budget commission for that cycle in the same manner as any other commissioner, and the applicable district grouping shall select its Representative pursuant to subsection (c). (3) The district grouping not represented by the vice chair shall select its Representative pursuant to subsection (c) and subsection (d), regardless of whether the vice chair serves under paragraph (1) of this subsection.

P-012.locator: p.5, lines 37-45, Sec. 2-263(f) County manager and CFO
P-012.text: (f) Administrative duties of the county manager and chief financial officer. The county manager and the chief financial officer shall retain administrative responsibility for budget preparation and presentation, including preparing budget documents, soliciting budget proposals from county departments, scheduling administrative budget meetings, and hosting meetings with departments to discuss proposed budgets and priorities.

P-013.locator: p.6, lines 2-23, Sec. 2-263(g) Duties of commissioner members
P-013.text: (g) Duties of commissioner members. The Northern Representative and Southern Representative shall: (1) solicit budget priorities, requests, and concerns from all members of the board of commissioners, including those not serving on the budget commission, through individual meetings, written submissions, or regular check-ins; (2) represent the interests and priorities of their respective district grouping throughout the budget development process; (3) participate directly and continuously with the county manager and chief financial officer throughout the budget development process, including review of departmental requests, revenue and expenditure assumptions, specific budgetary requests from other elected officials, and capital planning; (4) report periodically to the full board of commissioners on the status of budget development; and (5) participate with the county manager and chief financial officer in preparing the recommended budget for presentation to the full board of commissioners.

P-014.text: (h) Decision-making; advisory nature. (1) The budget commission shall operate by consensus rather than as a formal voting body as it works toward a joint budgetary presentation to the full board. (2) Where differences arise or consensus on an issue cannot be reached, the County Manager shall determine the best approach forward for presenting a proposed budget to the full board of commissioners. (3) Nothing in this code section shall be construed to grant the budget commission authority to adopt, amend, or approve the County budget. Final authority to adopt the annual budget remains exclusively with the full board of commissioners, consistent with O.C.G.A. § 36-81-1 et seq. and other applicable law.

P-015.locator: pp.6-7, Sec. 2-263(i)-(j) Presentation and meeting schedule
P-015.text: (i) Presentation to the board of commissioners. The recommended budget developed by the budget commission shall be presented jointly to the full board of commissioners by the county manager, the chief financial officer, the Northern Representative, and the Southern Representative, in accordance with the applicable budget calendar. (j) Meeting schedule. The budget commission shall convene on a schedule established by the county manager and chief financial officer in accordance with the applicable budget calendar.

P-027.text: A RESOLUTION TO ENSURE TRANSPARENCY AND INFORMED DECISION- MAKING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FULTON COUNTY BUDGET; TO PROHIBIT ACROSS-THE-BOARD CAPS ON DEPARTMENTAL BUDGET REQUESTS; TO REMOVE THE 5% CAP PLACED ON ALL FULTON COUNTY DEPARTMENTS FOR THE 2027 BUDGET; TO REQUIRE THAT ALL DEPARTMENTAL BUDGET REQUESTS ARE DISCLOSED IN THE PROPOSED BUDGET; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.

P-028.text: WHEREAS, the Fulton County Board of Commissioners recognizes that across- the-board spending cuts and spending caps are not the best method for controlling costs in the long run as they allow legacy spending in some departments to go unchecked while new and often necessary funding is denied; and WHEREAS, the Government Finance Officers Association identifies across-the- board spending cuts or caps as a symptom of weak budget development practices, stating that they are “a symptom of a budget process that does not provide a means for precisely targeted reductions”; and WHEREAS, The Pew Charitable Trusts has advised state and local leaders to “resist the temptation to make indiscriminate, across-the-board budget cuts” and instead use data and evidence to make strategic decisions about the allocation of limited public resources; and WHEREAS, Fulton County has traditionally included departmental budget “enhancement requests” in its publicly available Proposed Budget, which has allowed the Board of Commissioners to get a true picture of the departments’ needs and to make adjustments to the budget based on these requests; and WHEREAS, from FY2025 to FY2026, the percent change in Fulton County’s departmental budgets ranged from a decrease of 4 percent to an increase of 43 percent, which demonstrates the significant variation in the budgetary needs of individual departments; and

P-029.locator: p.2, lines 1-17 (WHEREAS clauses on the 5% cap)
P-029.text: WHEREAS, the newly established Budget Commission has restricted all departments to making budget requests that do not exceed 5% of their “base budget” for 2027 and only allows departments to describe broader needs in narrative form; and WHEREAS, during the FY2026 budget process, 27 of the county’s 41 General Fund departments and agencies submitted budget enhancement requests exceeding 5% of their base budgets and 14 of them received budget increases that exceeded 5%; and WHEREAS, Fulton County Code Section 2-261 requires the Budget Commission’s submission of the proposed budget to include the budget requests of the County’s departments, agencies, elected officials, and authorities that receive funding through the budget process; and WHEREAS, by placing the 5% cap on departmental enhancement requests, the Budget Commission is effectively making its mandate to submit a proposed budget that includes the budget requests of the County’s departments impossible; and WHEREAS, the Budget Commission failed to uphold its required duty to "solicit budget priorities, requests, and concerns from all members of the board of commissioners, including those not serving on the budget commission" in implementing this unprecedented restriction on the departments; and

P-030.locator: pp.2-4, proposed new wording of Sec. 2-261 (as proposed: struck words dropped)
P-030.text: Sec. 2-261, - Proposal and adoption of the budget. The budget commission shall submit or cause to be submitted annually to the board of commissioners, by no later than November 15, a proposed budget governing expenditures of all county funds, including capital outlay and public works projects, for the following year. The budget commission’s submission of the proposed budget shall include all budget requests of all of the county's departments, agencies, elected officials and authorities who receive funding from the county through the budget process. No limits or caps shall be placed on what a department, agency, elected official, or authority can request. This proposed budget will serve, as presented, as the operating budget until a final budget is adopted. The procedures for budget preparation, submission to the governing authority, review by the governing authority, public review, notice, and hearings shall be as provided for in Chapter 81 of Title 36 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36- 81-1 et seq.]. The budget shall then be adopted by the board of commissioners by no later than the second regular meeting in January of the year to which it applies, which budget, when so adopted by the board of commissioners, shall constitute the board of commissioners' appropriation of all funds for such year. The county manager is authorized to take all administrative steps necessary to implement the budget as approved. The budget so adopted may be revised during the year only by formal action of the board of commissioners in a regular meeting which has been advertised in accordance with subsection (e) of Code Section 36-81-5 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36-81-5] and no increase shall be made in such budget without provision also being made for financing such increase. The proposed budget submitted by the budget commission shall be accompanied by a report containing information and data required by subsection (b) of Code Section 36-81-5 of the O.C.G.A. [O.C.G.A. § 36-81-5]. A copy of the proposed budget shall be transmitted to the county clerk of the commission of Fulton County on the date it is submitted to the board of commissioners. Upon adoption of the budget, a copy shall be transmitted to the county clerk of the commission of Fulton County.
P-030.note: Removed the page numbers '[2]' and '[3]' at the page breaks. In the draft, 'the' is struck and 'all' underlined on p.3 line 3, and the sentence 'No limits or caps shall be placed on what a department, agency, elected official, or authority can request.' is underlined (new).

P-031.locator: p.4, lines 6-11 (requests left out because of the cap)
P-031.text: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that all of the county's departments, agencies, elected officials and authorities who receive funding from the county through the budget process shall be given the opportunity to submit any budget enhancement request for FY2027 that was omitted due to the 5% cap and shall have those requests included in the FY2027 Proposed Budget that will be presented to the Board of Commissioners on November 15, 2026.

P-083.text: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Fulton County Board of Commissioners amends F.C.C. Sec. 2-261 to clarify that all departmental budget requests are included in the proposed budget as follows:

P-084.locator: p.4, lines 12-20 (severability, effective date, adoption line)
P-084.text: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that if any section, subsection, paragraph, sentence, clause, or phrase of this Resolution is for any reason held to be invalid or unconstitutional, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this Resolution. BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that this Resolution shall become effective immediately upon adoption, and all other resolutions and parts of resolutions in conflict with this Resolution are hereby repealed to the extent of such conflict. PASSED AND ADOPTED by the Board of Commissioners of Fulton County, Georgia, this ____ day of ________________, 2026.

P-036.text: 26-0748 Board of Commissioners Public Comment - Citizens are allowed to voice County related opinions, concerns, requests, etc. during the Public Comment portion of the Commission meeting. Priority for public comment will be given to Fulton County citizens and those individuals representing businesses or organizations located within Fulton County, including their employees, whether such persons are commenting in-person, via emails or via Zoom or other electronic media (i.e., phone call). Non-Fulton County citizens will only be heard after all in-person Fulton County citizens, representatives of business and organizations located within Fulton County, including their employees, have been heard and the time allotted for public comment has not expired, except as otherwise provided in this code section. County staff shall verify the residency of each public speaker prior to such person being heard by the board. Speakers will be granted up to two minutes each. Members of the public will not be allowed to yield or donate time to other speakers. The Public Comment portion of the meeting will not exceed sixty (60) minutes at the First Regular Meeting, nor will this portion exceed sixty (60) minutes at the Second Regular Meeting. In the event the 60-minute time limit is reached prior to public comments being completed, public comment will be suspended and the business portion of the BOC meeting will commence. Public comment will resume at the end of the meeting. For more information or to arrange a speaking date, contact the Clerk’s Office.

P-045.text: Fulton County operates from a calendar year budget. Budgets are adopted annually for the General Fund and other specialty funds. Adopted budget documents are provided below. Budget Performance Reporting Strategic Plan 2026 FY 2026 Fulton County Adopted Budget FY2026 Fulton County Proposed Budget FY2026 Fulton County Government Revised Proposed Budget FY2026 Fulton County Government Revised Budget Presentation

P-046.text: Fulton County’s Fiscal Year 2026 Final Adopted Budget was approved by the Board of Commissioners on January 21, 2026. This budget includes all recommendations outlined in the Fiscal Year 2026 Proposed Budget provided on November 15, 2025, presented on November 19, 2025, and amendments approved on January 21, 2026. In this booklet, you will find the budget message submitted to the Board as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 Proposed Budget, and additional memos describing all modifications to that budget.
P-046.note: Widened in revision 2 to include the sentence saying the book reprints the budget message submitted with the FY2026 proposed budget.

P-047.text: WHEREAS, Fulton County's County Manager submitted a proposed budget to the Board of Commissioners on November 15th, 2025, as required under the County's Budget Ordinance, and WHEREAS, Fulton County's Board of Commissioners held a public hearing, as required by O.C.G.A. § 36-81-5, at a meeting on December 3, 2025, and WHEREAS, O.C.G.A. § 36-81-6 requires that on a date after the conclusion of the hearing, the governing authority adopt a budget ordinance or resolution making appropriations in such sums as the governing authority may deem sufficient, whether greater or less than the sums presented in the proposed budget.
P-047.note: This page is a signed scan; its text layer omits the space after 'WHEREAS,' on line 6. Checked against the rendered page image.

P-048.text: In January 2025, the County entered into an agreement with the United States Department of Justice to address constitutional violations at the Fulton County Jail and mandated the County implement specific reforms to improve jail conditions, including providing better safety from violence, ensuring adequate medical and mental health care, improving staffing and supervision, and creating sanitary and humane living conditions. We were challenged with navigating consent decree compliance while continuing to recover from our 2024 cybersecurity incident.

P-049.locator: p.8 (budget message): hearings and enhancement requests (repeated on p.19)
P-049.text: The County reinstated formal budget hearings allowing department and agencies the platform to review current and historical personnel and operating data to identify key spending trends. The hearings also presented a platform for our partners to communicate opportunities, challenges and prioritize their additional financial requests (if any). Even with the efforts to reprioritize current resources, the county received hundreds of operating and capital enhancements. All submissions were received and carefully reviewed, however many included investment requests for enhanced programming with recurring costs. The volume of requests coupled with known budget pressures and financial resources resulted in many unmet requests. Working within the current financial constraints, a rules-based criterion which first categorized enhancements based on contractual, regulatory, statutory, board action, inflationary drivers and cybersecurity was utilized in evaluating additional investments above a department’s recurring base budget. We’ve continued utilization of non-recurring revenue for recurring costs where available, however there were no additional resources available to fund program enhancements above and beyond the increased costs for maintaining a current service level. This further emphasizes that additional resources will be needed for consent decree compliance. The enhancement submissions are included as an appendix and are categorized in tranches including Sheriff, Justice and Safety, Health and Human Services, Infrastructure and Economic Development and Open and Responsible Government.

P-050.locator: p.21 (budget message): consent decree costs and a 1% reduction
P-050.text: • Consent Decree: Includes funding of $31.8 million in Board approved consent decree costs. While over $30 million is included in the 2026 budget, costs could exceed a range from $30 - $60 million. To date, all decree compliance related costs are still being vetted and have not been determined, but as costs accelerate from partial year to full year recurring implementation, this number is expected to grow. Additional costs will be presented to the Board for consideration when available. • 1% Reduction across all Agencies/Departments: Includes a decrease of $10 million in the general fund budget by instituting a 1% decrease across all agencies and departments. Appointing Authorities will be able to review their remaining resources to determine impact.

P-051.locator: p.33 (budget message): requests beyond the proposal
P-051.text: In addition to the above-mentioned enhancements already considered, there were almost $158 million in unique personnel/operating requests and over $64 million in capital requests received from departments, agencies and external stakeholders during the FY2026 budget process. The requests were separately reviewed and categorized into tranches for funding consideration if additional resources are realized at the end of 2025.

P-101.locator: p.20 (budget message): property tax as the main revenue; when the 2026 tax rate (millage rate) is set
P-101.text: The County’s primary source of revenue is property tax. The FY2026 current year property tax revenue projection assumes a flat millage rate of 8.87 as provided by the Board of Commissioners when setting the FY2025 millage rate. The final determination of the FY2026 millage rate by the Board of Commissioners will take place during the summer of 2026.

P-103.text: This $1.4 billion budget reflects both, the needs of our residents and a steady operational and fiscally responsible plan.

P-069.locator: article, paragraphs 1-3 (news conference, letter, who attended)
P-069.text: Fulton County justice officials are pushing back against proposed changes to next year’s budget process, warning that funding decisions could affect court delays, jail conditions and public safety. County leaders held a news conference on the steps of the Fulton County Courthouse Wednesday morning and sent a detailed letter to the Board of Commissioners outlining their requests. Officials unite on budget requests The sheriff, district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk, probate judge and public defender attended the news conference.

P-070.locator: article, paragraphs 4-5 (what the group asked for)
P-070.text: The group is asking commissioners to wait until January to approve the county’s 2027 spending plan, which would give incoming board members a say in the budget. A January vote is normal protocol, but current law does not prohibit commissioners from voting earlier. The officials are also calling for more funding to address what they describe as staffing shortages, court delays and jail overcrowding.

P-071.text: Fulton County Solicitor General Keith Gammage said his office is underfunded. “Each year we are underfunded. My office is just one example. I’ll give you one more: We have a lack of law-enforcement investigators. What that is causing, is one investigator to carry a caseload - upwards of 400,” Gammage said.

P-072.text: Fulton County Board Commissioner Dana Barrett, District 3, alleged some current board members are trying to take control of the budget process. “There are some shenanigans among some of the current board members who are angling to take control of the budget process in a way that I feel is inappropriate,” Barrett said. Barrett named Commissioner Bob Ellis and Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman, saying they are “creating a budget commission that only they qualify to be on.”

P-073.locator: article, Commissioner Bob Ellis; Vice Chair not reached
P-073.text: Commissioner Bob Ellis responded to the allegation. “We have a budget commission. Those meetings are open meetings. They are speaking and addressing the budget commission just like a standard committee structure, but all commissioners and their staff are able to attend and hear what is said,” Ellis said. “The process we’ve laid out is more transparent and open than anything we’ve had in recent years,” Ellis said. Ellis also said there is no talk of an early vote. Atlanta News First is still waiting to hear back from Commissioner Khadijah Abdur-Rahman.

P-076.text: The coalition calling themselves "Justice Leaders," which includes the sheriff, district attorney, superior court clerk, solicitor general, probate court chief judge and public defender, announced Wednesday that they will not attend scheduled budget hearings starting next week. Leaders sent a joint letter and held a news conference outlining their decision to decline live presentations. Their primary objection centers on a new framework that require department heads to present critical funding needs to a two-commissioner panel rather than the full board. Under the current structure, District 2 Commissioner Bob Ellis and District 6 Commissioner Khadijah Abdur-Rahman sit on the Budget Commission. The panel evaluates department requests and makes recommendations for the final budget but does not possess final voting power.

P-077.locator: article, the 5% directive and Solicitor-General Gammage
P-077.text: The justice leaders also raised concerns over a directive asking all county departments to limit any request for additional funding to 5% above current allocations for the upcoming 2027 billion-dollar-plus budget. "We believe it to be our duty to call attention to what we believe to be a lack of proper investment in the entire ecosystem of the courts," said Fulton County Solicitor General Keith Gammage.

P-078.locator: article, Chief Probate Judge Johnson and Sheriff Labat
P-078.text: Fulton County Chief Probate Judge Kenya Johnson, speaking on behalf of the coalition, stated that the group respectfully declines to participate in a format that limits the voices of the justice system. "We respectfully decline to participate in a process that unnecessarily limits the voices of the justice system," Johnson said. Sheriff Patrick Labat criticized the two-commissioner arrangement as unfair to county agencies and taxpayers. "For two commissioners to take a hold of this project—hijack this process is simply unfair," Labat said.

P-079.text: Commissioner Bob Ellis addressed the coalition's concerns, noting that the Budget Commission is solely responsible for drafting recommendations and that the full Board of Commissioners will review and vote on the final budget.

P-080.locator: article, written submissions; the story's sources and correction
P-080.text: Despite refusing to appear in person for next week's hearings, all participating justice department leaders confirmed they have submitted their formal 2027 budget requests in writing. The Source: The information in this story was gathered from a news conference and letter issued by Fulton County Justice Leaders, statements from Probate Court Chief Judge Kenya Johnson, Sheriff Patrick Labat, Commissioner Bob Ellis, Solicitor General Keith Gammage, and Clerk Che Alexander, as reported by FOX 5 Atlanta reporter Aungelique Proctor. The original story has been updated since publication to correct Judge Kenya Johnson's name.

P-082.text: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners voted 4-1 to reestablish a Budget Commission, with Commissioner Marvin Arrington Jr. abstaining and Commissioner Dana Barrett absent for the vote.

paras: Each round runs the same checks. A page passes a round only when every check passes. After that, we fix only sentences that misstate a source or break our writing rules, and a fresh checker looks again at just those sentences. Other suggestions wait for the next full round.

sections.title: What's still open
paras: These suggestions would change a card, a label or the balance between sides, so they wait for the next full round. Some contradict each other; we list both views rather than pick one quietly.
items: Reviewers disagree on how to describe the Budget Commission's role. One says "helps draft" understates it; the other says "the commission alone drafts" overstates it.
Card 3's evidence label: one reviewer wants it to use the county code's exact words, and the other wants it to stress that the code says the draft "shall include" every department's requests.
County records could add to both sides: the duties the code gives the two commissioners, and the 2026 budget's unmet requests and thin savings.
The cards should use one rule for where a side's own figures go.
Several lines can be plainer, and some evidence labels are long.
Nobody has transcribed the Board's meeting videos, where commissioners may have explained their votes. The proposal due Nov 15 isn't public yet; when it is, several "Uncertain" labels can be settled.
